documents.title: Our AI Policy (Writing Center)
documents.stance_why: The page sets no ban or permission of its own. It says 'our support aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor for that class and the individual assignment', handing the decision to instructors, so the stance is delegates. It also welcomes AI as 'valuable tools' where allowed.
documents.summary: The University of Miami Writing Center states how its consultants handle AI: they follow each instructor's and publication's rules, may recommend AI tools only where allowed, and emphasize ethics, attribution and critical thinking. It is a unit-level statement, not a university-wide policy, and it discloses that ChatGPT helped draft it.

units.why: The opening says AI 'can be valuable tools for writing and research', the Writing Center's positive view of AI. It is a statement of benefit, not a rule, so P87 rather than the default-stance type P02.
units.anchor: artificial intelligences (AIs) can be valuable tools for writing and research

units.why: Says writers 'will need to be able to effectively and ethically engage with these tools inside and outside of academia', a professional-readiness reason for engaging with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: writers will need to be able to effectively and ethically engage with these tools

units.why: 'our support aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor for that class and the individual assignment': the Center defers the AI rule to each instructor and assignment, so P04.
units.anchor: our support aligns with the guidelines and expectations set by each professor

units.why: For publication work consultants 'align our support with the professional guidelines for that publication', deferring to venue rules, which P62 names. Closest type, but it is about clients' publications, not theses or grants.
units.anchor: align our support with the professional guidelines for that publication
units.frag_start: When clients are working towards publications,
units.fit_note: Covers deferring to a publication's guidelines for clients' writing, not theses, grants or peer review specifically.

units.why: Asks instructors 'to be clear about your expectations for student use of AI, ideally in writing, either in your syllabus or on your assignment sheet', addressed to instructors, so P09.
units.anchor: Please be clear about your expectations for student use of AI, ideally in writing
units.fit_note: A request ('ideally in writing'), not a firm requirement, and justified so that Writing Center staff can follow it.

units.why: Asks students to 'be aware of your instructor's AI expectations' at sessions, a duty to know the rules that apply, so P78 rather than P10 (which is about asking when unsure).
units.anchor: Please be aware of your instructor's AI expectations when meeting with your writing center consultant

units.why: 'please bring them to your session': students with written instructor AI guidelines are asked to bring them, a step to make the rules visible to the consultant. Nearest type is P78.
units.anchor: AI guidelines from your instructor in writing, please bring them to your session.
units.fit_note: Asks students to bring written instructor guidelines to a session so consultants can follow them; goes beyond knowing the rules.

units.why: 'We will work within the specific guidelines provided by instructors for each class and assignment' repeats the deferral to instructor rules as a Center value under its own heading, so P04. Not an exact repeat: it adds the heading and the commitment form.
units.anchor: We will work within the specific guidelines provided by instructors for each class and assignment
units.frag_start: We will work within the specific

units.why: 'Consultants will not recommend AI tools to students that violate instructors' expectations or academic integrity' limits what staff may recommend. Nearest type is P59 (staff AI-related work), with a fit note.
units.anchor: Consultants will not recommend AI tools to students that violate instructors' expectations or academic integrity.
units.fit_note: Concerns which AI tools staff may recommend to students, not staff's own AI use.

units.why: 'When allowable and appropriate, our consultants may recommend AI tools and help students evaluate the results' permits staff to recommend AI, conditional on it being allowed.
units.anchor: When allowable and appropriate, our consultants may recommend AI tools
units.fit_note: Staff recommending AI tools to students, not staff's own AI use.

units.why: 'help students evaluate the results' of AI tools is staff support for critically evaluating AI output, which P31 covers; it is phrased as staff help, not as a student duty.
units.frag_start: consultants may recommend AI tools and
units.fit_note: Staff help students evaluate AI output; the passage does not state a student duty to verify.

units.why: 'Our primary goal is, as always, to help students learn how to grow as writers' gives the learning purpose that frames the Center's AI approach. Nearest type is P41, though the passage does not say AI shortcuts practice.
units.anchor: Our primary goal is, as always, to help students learn how to grow as writers.
units.fit_note: States that skill growth is the goal; does not say AI use undermines practice.

units.why: 'learning to leverage AI responsibly to improve their writing, research, evaluation, and revision skills' welcomes AI for writing and revision at stages of the writing process, so P91.
units.anchor: learning to leverage AI responsibly to improve their writing, research, evaluation, and revision skills

units.why: 'We continue to focus on writing practices and critical thinking in all our sessions' says sessions keep centering the student's own thinking, so P32 (student stays primary thinker), as a description of Center practice.
units.anchor: We continue to focus on writing practices and critical thinking in all our sessions.
units.fit_note: Describes the Center's focus, not a rule on students.

units.why: 'We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use' invites ethical reflection, which P53 covers. It is an encouragement, hence 'should'.
units.anchor: We encourage writers at all levels to consider the ethical dimensions of AI use

units.why: 'emphasizing original work, attribution and citation when appropriate' asks for acknowledging AI use and original work. Attribution is the more specific ask, so P24 over P29.
units.anchor: emphasizing original work, attribution and citation when appropriate
units.fit_note: Attribution is 'when appropriate', and original work (P29) is emphasized in the same phrase.

units.why: 'an understanding of AI's limitations, biases, and environmental impacts' names limits, bias and environmental costs students should understand, so P53.
units.anchor: an understanding of AI's limitations, biases, and environmental impacts

units.why: 'guiding students in integrating AI tools in ways that enhance their learning experience while upholding the values and expectations of their instructors' says staff may help students integrate AI under instructor expectations, so a conditional permission (P02 nearest).
units.anchor: guiding students in integrating AI tools in ways that enhance their learning experience
units.frag_start: In some cases, that may mean
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on instructor and university expectations and is framed as staff guidance, not a default rule.

units.why: 'This statement was constructed with input from ChatGPT 4o' discloses the Center's own AI use in drafting the policy. Nearest type is P47 (disclosing AI use to students).
units.anchor: This statement was constructed with input from ChatGPT 4o
units.fit_note: Disclosure of AI use in drafting the policy statement itself, not in grading, feedback or instruction.

notes: Only the Writing Center page was included; the collector found no university-wide, school or computing policy. Several units carry fit_notes because the page is about staff support, not student rules.
